  • Rumen: Largest compartment; site of microbial fermentation
  • Reticulum: "Honeycomb" stomach; traps hardware (nails, wire)

  • Omasum: Water absorption compartment, not the true stomach.

posts.post_content: Incisors are absent in upper jaw and their place is taken by dental pad in which animal?

Correct Answer: All Ruminants

posts.post_title: Temperature Zones for Livestock and Poultry
posts.post_content:

1. Thermo-neutral zone for pig & cattle(a) 21-24°C
2. Thermo-neutral zone for poultry(b) 21.1°C

posts.post_title: Most Prolific Sheep and Goat Breeds

posts.post_content: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?

posts.post_content: An average number of days between latest two successive calving dates for all cows in the herd is known as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

  • Calving interval: Interval between two successive calvings of a SINGLE animal (individual measure)
  • Calving index: Average interval between two successive calvings of the HERD (herd measure)
  • Generation interval: Average age of parents when their offspring are born
  • Herd average: Average milk production of a herd
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Calving interval: Refers to individual animal, not the whole herd average.
  • Generation interval: Related to age of parents at offspring birth, not calving.

posts.post_title: Main Cause of Newborn Pig Mortality
posts.post_content: Newborn pig mortality is mainly due to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Crushing by mother

The main cause of newborn pig mortality is crushing by mother. Sows are large and heavy animals, and they can accidentally crush piglets while lying down, especially in the first few days after farrowing.

Prevention

Farrowing pens with guard rails are used to prevent crushing of piglets. Guard rails are fixed along the walls of the farrowing pen at a height and distance that allows piglets to escape underneath while preventing the sow from lying directly against the wall.

Related Pig Terminology
  • Crit/Card/Runt: Smallest piglet in a litter, usually last to be farrowed
  • Farrowing: Act of parturition in pigs
  • Sow: Adult female pig
Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Piglet anemia: Common condition but not the main cause of mortality.
  • Cannibalism: Can occur but is less common than crushing.
  • Enteritis: Intestinal inflammation occurs but is not the leading cause.

posts.post_title: Timing of Dipping in Relation to Shearing
posts.post_content: Dipping should be done:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Immediately before shearing

Dipping should be done immediately before shearing. This ensures that:

  • The insecticide reaches the skin through the full fleece, killing parasites at the skin surface
  • The fleece is cleaned of dirt and waste before being shorn and sold
  • Any parasites lurking in the wool are eliminated before the wool is removed
Why NOT After Shearing?

After shearing, the skin is exposed and may have small nicks or cuts from the shearing process. Applying chemical dip immediately after shearing can cause skin irritation and chemical burns on the freshly exposed skin.

Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • At any time: Timing matters — before shearing is optimal.
  • Immediately after shearing: Risk of skin irritation and chemical burns.
  • During rainy season: Not the standard timing recommendation.

posts.post_content: Canine teeth are absent in:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Both a & b

Canine teeth are absent in both Cattle (all ruminants) and Mare (female horse).

  • Cattle: All ruminants lack canine teeth — dental formula 2(I 0/4, C 0/0, PM 3/3, M 3/3) = 32 teeth.
  • Mare: Female horse lacks canines — dental formula 2(I 3/3, C 0/0, PM 3/3, M 3/3) = 36 teeth.
Key Distinction

The stallion (male horse) DOES have canine teeth: 2(I 3/3, C 1/1, PM 3/3, M 3/3) = 40 teeth. This 4-tooth difference (40 - 36 = 4 canines) is the sex-based dental distinction in horses.

Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Cattle alone: Correct but incomplete — mare also lacks canines.
  • Mare alone: Correct but incomplete — cattle also lacks canines.
  • Stallion: Stallion HAS canine teeth (1 per quadrant = 4 total).

posts.post_title: Floor Slope in Tail to Tail System
posts.post_content: The desirable slope of floor in tail to tail system is:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: 1:40

The desirable slope of floor in the tail to tail (face-out) system is 1:40, which equals 1 inch per 10 feet length (Table 36 notes).

Double Row Housing Types
  • Face to face (Face in): Animals face each other with a common feed alley in the centre
  • Tail to tail (Face out): Animals face outward with a common dung channel in the centre — preferred for hygiene
Advantages of Tail to Tail System
  • Lesser danger of spread of disease (animals don't breathe into each other's faces)

Why Other Options Are Wrong

posts.post_content: Maintenance of lactation is termed as:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

Galactopoiesis is the maintenance of lactation — the process of sustaining milk secretion once it has been initiated.

  • Mammogenesis: Growth and development of the mammary gland
  • Lactogenesis: Initiation of milk secretion (onset of lactation)
  • Galactopoiesis: Maintenance of lactation (keeping milk production going)
Sequence

Mammogenesis (gland development) → Lactogenesis (milk secretion starts) → Galactopoiesis (lactation maintained).

Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Mammogenesis: Growth/development of mammary gland, not maintenance of lactation.
  • Lactogenesis: Initiation (start) of milk secretion, not maintenance.
  • Lactation: General term for the process of producing milk, not specifically "maintenance."

posts.post_content: The most popular fine wool-producing breed of sheep in the world is:

posts.post_content: "Sheep-like goat" is __________ and "goat-like sheep" is __________:

Angora goat (Turkey) is known as "sheep-like goat" because of its Mohair (white, soft, silky hairs) that resembles sheep wool (Table 24). Nellore sheep (AP) is known as "goat-like sheep" because it has no wool — it appears more like a goat (Table 23).

posts.post_title: Purpose of Guard Rails in Farrowing Pen
posts.post_content: Farrowing pen with guard rails is necessary to:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:
Correct Answer: Avoid crushing of piglets

Farrowing pens with guard rails are specifically designed to avoid crushing of piglets by the sow. Guard rails are horizontal bars fixed around the inside walls of the pen at a height of about 20-25 cm, creating a safe space where piglets can escape when the sow lies down.

Why This Is Important

Crushing by the mother is the leading cause of newborn pig mortality. The sow weighs several hundred kilograms and can easily kill a piglet weighing just 1-2 kg by lying on it.

Why Other Options Are Wrong
  • Control parasites: Guard rails have no role in parasite control.
  • Avoid crowding: Guard rails don't address overcrowding; proper stocking density does.
  • Avoid disease outbreak: Disease prevention requires biosecurity measures, not guard rails.

posts.post_content: Which of the following is/are true about shearing in sheep?

posts.post_content: Castration of female animal is known as:

posts.post_title: Cattle Shed Arrangement for Disease Prevention

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

  • Face to face: Convenient for feed distribution; animals face each other (higher disease risk)

posts.post_title: Reuff’s Method of Casting – Applicable Animals

Reuff's method is the most common and efficient method of casting (restraining by bringing the animal to the ground) of cattle and buffalo. It involves tying a long rope around the animal's body in a specific pattern to safely bring it down for surgical procedures or examinations.

  • Casting = bringing an animal to the ground for restraint during procedures
  • Reuff's method is specifically designed for large ruminants (cattle & buffalo)

  • Horse: Different casting methods are used for horses (e.g., side-line method).

posts.post_content: The mohair-producing breed of goat is:

  • Angora → Mohair (Turkey)

posts.post_content: Cattle has how many times more number of sweat glands than buffalo?

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

posts.post_title: Horned Rams and Polled Ewes Sheep Breed

posts.post_title: Shortest Generation Interval in Meat Livestock

posts.post_title: Differences Between Zebu Cattle and Buffalo
posts.post_content: Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?

_aimcq_options.text: Zebu cattle are humped while buffalo & exotic cattle are humpless
The dewlap is present in cattle while absent in buffalo
Cattle horns are rounded while buffalo horns are compressed

Correct Answer: All the above

ALL statements are true regarding differences between Zebu cattle, exotic cattle, and buffalo:

  • Zebu cattle are humped; buffalo & exotic cattle are humpless: The hump is a distinguishing feature of Zebu (Bos indicus) cattle. Exotic cattle (Bos taurus) and buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) lack this hump.
  • Dewlap is present in cattle, absent in buffalo: The dewlap (loose skin fold under the neck) is characteristic of cattle, especially Zebu breeds. It is well-developed in Zebu cattle but less developed in exotic cattle.
  • Cattle horns are rounded; buffalo horns are compressed: Cross-section of cattle horns is circular/rounded, while buffalo horns have a flat/compressed cross-section.

posts.post_title: Facts About Foot-Bath in Sheep Farms
posts.post_content: Which of the following is/are true about foot-bath in sheep farms?

_aimcq_options.text: It is used to control FMD & foot-rot disease
It is most effective in monsoon season
It is provided at the entrance of the farm to control the spread of contagious disease

  • Most effective in monsoon: Foot-rot is most prevalent during wet/monsoon season when the ground is damp and muddy, promoting bacterial growth.
  • Placed at farm entrance: Animals walk through the foot-bath when entering or leaving the farm, ensuring their hooves are disinfected and preventing spread of contagious diseases.

The disinfectant of choice during FMD outbreak is 4% Na₂CO₃ (Sodium Carbonate).

posts.post_title: Best Age for Dehorning in Calf

  • Chemical method: KOH (Caustic Potash) is applied to the horn bud

posts.post_content: The breed of cattle producing highest milk yield and lowest milk fat is:

posts.post_title: Best Method of Drying Off Dairy Cow

posts.post_title: Orientation of Poultry and Animal Houses

posts.post_content: Zebu cattle can be distinguished from exotic cattle by the presence of:

meta_input._aimcq_explanation:

posts.post_content: Just prior to breeding season, shearing of sheep flock is important because:

posts.post_content: Commonly used chemical for dehorning is:

posts.post_content: In cattle rearing (dairy), feed cost alone accounts for what percentage of total farm expenses?
